question_text: A government employee is facing an administrative complaint for dishonesty. The investigating committee did not allow her to present witnesses or cross-examine the complainant. She argues that her right to due process was violated. Under Article III of the 1987 Constitution, which of the following is correct?

options.text: Due process is not required in administrative cases because they are not criminal in nature.
Due process requires that she be given the opportunity to present her case, including presenting witnesses and cross-examining the complainant.
Due process only requires that she be notified of the complaint, not that she be allowed to present evidence.
Due process is satisfied as long as the committee is impartial.
